QUOTE: "By default it expands `ctx->MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(state)` to `ctx->private_state`, so the member is renamed. Code that writes `ssl->state` against the public header fails to compile. The renaming is the whole mechanism: the struct layout is unchanged, but the name a caller can type is no longer the real one."
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer says the compile-time enforcement works by renaming the member, with the struct layout unchanged. It does not use the words "visible and sized", but it says the same thing.
